newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Two Koreas to hold Red Cross talks in Beijing.
newsitem.headline: Two Koreas to hold Red Cross talks in Beijing.

text.p: The first inter-Korean Red Cross talks in almost five years aimed at speeding food aid to the hungry North will be held in Beijing on Saturday, a South Korean Red Cross statement said on Wednesday.
The two sides had been bickering over where to hold the session, with the North insisting on Beijing and the South on the border village of Panmunjom.

"I don't think it is desirable to stall the meeting any longer over a decision on the venue," the president of South Korea's Red Cross was quoted as saying in a message to his Northern counterpart, accepting the North's demand.
Kang Young-hoon said the Southern side would send three representatives plus three aides and he asked North Korea to choose an exact time and place.
The message was relayed via a telephone hot line at Panmunjom, the only border crossing point.
The last inter-Korean Red Cross talks were in August, 1992, in Panmunjom.
A National Unification Ministry statement said Saturday's meeting would discuss procedures for transporting and distributing food, not the size or timing of aid.
South Korea's Red Cross is the only window for private food donations to the North.
International aid groups say that North Korea, hit by devastating floods for two years in a row, is sliding into famine. Pyongyang has reported deaths of children from malnutrition.
Separately, the South Korean Red Cross said it delivered 1,380 tonnes of corn to North Korea by train on Wednesday.
It said the corn, worth 180 million won ($200,000), was donated by a Buddhist group and bought in China.

The South Korean Red Cross also plans to ship 110 tonnes of wheat flour worth 36 million won to the North later this week, Red Cross officials said. The aid was bought with money raised by a South Korean Christian group.
The two Koreas remain technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce.
